  - paragraph:
    - text: Stops the REST API from listing account login names to logged-out visitors. Without it, anyone can read

  - text: Require authentication for all REST requests

    - code: image.php
    - text: ", since the theme means to render them. Core has its own switch since 6.4 ("
    - code: wp_attachment_pages_enabled
    - text: ); this prefers the parent post over the bare file.
- text: Emoji Script
- group "Emoji Script":
  - text: Emoji Script
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - checkbox "Disable the emoji detection script" [checked]
    - text: Disable the emoji detection script
  - paragraph: Removes the emoji detection script and inline CSS from every page.
- text: Post Passwords
- group "Post Passwords":
  - text: Post Passwords
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - checkbox "Hide post password protection in the editor"
    - text: Hide post password protection in the editor
  - paragraph: Hides the "Password protected" visibility option in the editor. WordPress post passwords are weak and are bypassed by full-page caching, which serves the same cached page regardless. Existing password-protected posts keep their field so they stay editable. Off by default.
- text: Protected Search Results
- group "Protected Search Results":
  - text: Protected Search Results
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - checkbox "Hide password-protected posts from searches without access" [checked]
    - text: Hide password-protected posts from searches without access
  - paragraph: Keeps protected titles and excerpts out of site search unless the logged-in visitor can edit that post or has unlocked its password. Honors custom per-post capabilities and password-access filters. Does not change admin searches, direct links or stored content.
- text: Broken Shortcodes
- group "Broken Shortcodes":
  - text: Broken Shortcodes
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - checkbox "Hide recognizable missing-shortcode markup from readers" [checked]
    - text: Hide recognizable missing-shortcode markup from readers
  - paragraph: Keeps enclosed text and stored content. People who can edit the post still see the residue. Site Health reports recent affected posts and tag names without scanning posts. Bare bracketed words, code examples, registered shortcodes and REST output stay unchanged. Does not restore missing plugin output.
- text: Post Revision Retention
- group "Post Revision Retention":
  - text: Post Revision Retention
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - spinbutton "Post Revision Retention": "10"
    - text: revisions
  - paragraph:
    - text: Maximum revisions WordPress keeps for each post. Enter
    - code: "-1"
    - text: for unlimited or
    - code: "0"
    - text: to disable revisions. Changing this governs future saves; it does not immediately delete revisions already stored. A numeric or false
    - code: WP_POST_REVISIONS
    - text: value in
    - code: wp-config.php
    - text: takes precedence.
- heading "Editor" [level=2]
- text: Classic Editor
- group "Classic Editor":
  - text: Classic Editor
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - checkbox "Use the Classic editor instead of the block editor"
    - text: Use the Classic editor instead of the block editor
  - paragraph: Restores the pre-block editing experience for posts, pages, and custom post types, plus the classic Widgets screen. Front-end display of existing block content is unaffected, and on a block theme the Site Editor stays available. Off by default.
- heading "Media" [level=2]
- text: Upload Filenames
- group "Upload Filenames":
  - text: Upload Filenames
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - checkbox "Lowercase new upload filenames" [checked]
    - text: Lowercase new upload filenames
  - paragraph: Avoids case-sensitivity surprises when files move between case-insensitive local/staging and case-sensitive Linux production. On by default; only affects new uploads.
- text: Image Sizes
- group "Image Sizes":
  - text: Image Sizes
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - checkbox "Show generated image sizes on attachments" [checked]
    - text: Show generated image sizes on attachments
  - paragraph: Adds a read-only panel to the attachment edit screen listing each generated image size with its dimensions, file size, and URL — a quick way to confirm what WordPress produced. On by default.
- heading "Email" [level=2]
- text: Email Deliverability
- group "Email Deliverability":
  - text: Email Deliverability
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - checkbox "Warn when site email looks broken" [checked]
    - text: Warn when site email looks broken
  - paragraph: "Warns administrators when site email looks broken: a risky default From address (invalid, or an example/local/test domain) on a non-local site, and a bulk password reset that sent zero emails — replacing WordPress's misleading \"success\" notice. On by default."
- text: Non-Production Email
- group "Non-Production Email":
  - text: Non-Production Email
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - checkbox "Stop outgoing email unless this is the production site" [checked]
    - text: Stop outgoing email unless this is the production site
  - paragraph:
    - text: A database copied from production brings real addresses and whatever mail service production used. A cron run or a bulk action then emails real people from a staging site or a laptop. Does nothing on production, so it cannot be left on by mistake. Override per site with
    - code: KEEL_ALLOW_NONPRODUCTION_MAIL
    - text: in
    - code: wp-config.php
    - text: or the
    - code: keel_suppress_nonproduction_mail
    - text: filter.
- heading "Admin and Front-End UX" [level=2]
- text: Admin Search
- group "Admin Search":
  - text: Admin Search
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - checkbox "Search titles only in admin list tables"
    - text: Search titles only in admin list tables
  - paragraph: Speeds up admin list-table search on big sites by matching titles only.
- text: Front-End Admin Bar
- group "Front-End Admin Bar":
  - text: Front-End Admin Bar
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - combobox "Front-End Admin Bar":
      - option "Leave unchanged (WordPress default)" [selected]
      - option "Hide for non-admins"
      - option "Hide for everyone"
      - option "Auto-hide, reveal on hover or keyboard focus (desktop)"
  - paragraph: The WordPress toolbar shown across the top of the site for logged-in users. Hide it for non-admins or everyone, or auto-hide it so it slides out of the way and returns on hover or keyboard focus (desktop only).
- text: Admin Menu Width
- group "Admin Menu Width":
  - text: Admin Menu Width
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network" [checked]
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - combobox "Admin Menu Width":
      - option "Leave unchanged"
      - option "160px (WordPress default)"
      - option "200px"
      - option "240px" [selected]
      - option "280px"
      - option "300px"
  - paragraph: Sets the width of the left admin menu, useful when plugin menu labels are long. WordPress default is 160px. Leave unchanged and Keel sets no width at all; choose 160px to assert core's width over a theme, host, or plugin that has widened the menu.
- text: Admin List Tables
- group "Admin List Tables":
  - text: Admin List Tables
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - combobox "Admin List Tables":
      - option "Leave unchanged" [selected]
      - option "Tidy existing tables"
      - option "Tidy + helper columns"
  - paragraph: Tidy sizes columns to their content, simplifies headings and dates, and initially hides optional columns where you haven’t saved a preference. Tidy + helper columns also adds ID, Image and Modified to post lists, file size to Media, and registration and last-login dates to Users. Where you haven’t saved a preference, Image starts visible; ID and Modified stay off until you tick them in Screen Options. Your saved Screen Options stay unchanged; use Screen Options to show or hide individual columns.
- text: Environment Indicator
- group "Environment Indicator":
  - text: Environment Indicator
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - checkbox "Show the current environment in the admin bar"
    - text: Show the current environment in the admin bar
  - paragraph:
    - text: Adds a color-coded label to the admin bar showing the current environment (Production, Staging, Development, or Local) from
    - code: wp_get_environment_type()
    - text: ", or from the Environment setting below when one is chosen — a quick guard against acting on the wrong site. Common local-development hosts are recognized automatically. Off by default."
- text: Environment
- group "Environment":
  - text: Environment
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - combobox "Environment":
      - option "Automatic (WordPress environment type)" [selected]
      - option "Production"
      - option "Staging"
      - option "Development"
      - option "Local"
  - paragraph:
    - text: What Keel treats this site as, for the environment indicator and for holding back non-production email. Automatic reads
    - code: WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE
    - text: and recognizes common local-development hosts. Choose an environment to override that when the site is mislabeled — for example, a live site whose
    - code: wp-config.php
    - text: was copied from a local install and still says
    - code: local
    - text: ". This changes Keel only: WordPress and other plugins keep reading"
    - code: WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE
    - text: ", so fix that too."
- heading "Login and Sessions" [level=2]
- text: Remember Me
- group "Remember Me":
  - text: Remember Me
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - checkbox "Disable Remember Me and remove the login checkbox"
    - text: Disable Remember Me and remove the login checkbox
  - paragraph: Removes the Remember Me checkbox from the login form, so every login uses the regular session length below. Useful for shared or kiosk machines.
- text: Regular Session Length
- group "Regular Session Length":
  - text: Regular Session Length
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - spinbutton "Regular Session Length": "2"
    - text: days
  - paragraph: How long a normal (non-remembered) login stays signed in. WordPress's default is 2 days.
- text: Remember Me Length
- group "Remember Me Length":
  - text: Remember Me Length
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network" [checked]
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - spinbutton "Remember Me Length": "30"
    - text: days
  - paragraph: How long a remembered login stays signed in. WordPress's default is 14 days. It cannot be shorter than the regular session length above.
- heading "Branding" [level=2]
- text: Login Logo
- group "Login Logo":
  - text: Login Logo
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - combobox "Login Logo":
      - option "Keep the WordPress logo and wordpress.org link (WordPress default)" [selected]
      - option "Remove the logo and the wordpress.org link"
      - option "Keep the logo, drop the wordpress.org link"
      - option "Replace the logo with your site logo"
  - paragraph: The default logo links to wordpress.org, off your site. Left untouched by default, since changing the login screen out of the box is intrusive. Removing, unlinking, or replacing the logo always points the header link at your home page. Replacing uses the logo set in the Customizer, or the site icon if there is no logo; with neither set, the WordPress logo stays.
- heading "Performance" [level=2]
- text: Heartbeat API
- group "Heartbeat API":
  - text: Heartbeat API
  - checkbox "Decide this for the whole network"
  - text: Decide this for the whole network
  - paragraph:
    - checkbox "Slow background admin polling"
    - text: Slow background admin polling
  - paragraph: "Slows admin polling to 60 seconds and drops it on the dashboard home. Off by default: Heartbeat also powers autosave and post-lock warnings, so enabling this will make them update less often."
